title: A63 Analyst-Judgment Register row
description: Schema for one row of analysis/canonical/core_controls/A63_analyst_judgment_register.csv. New in v1.4.0 — closes the v1.3.6 output review #3.3 finding (analyst_judgment misuse). Pre-v1.4.0 every analyst_judgment claim was an A59 row with ClaimType=analyst_judgment + a JustificationRationale string referencing upstream ClaimIDs (INV-07). The bsa-no-new-claims-auditor checked AJ:C-xxx tags in H1/H4 for INV-07 conformance, but there was no separate register tracking which AJ claims had been validated, who authored them, or whether they had passed peer review. The reviewer's concern: AJ claims could compound on one another (chain of inference disguised as judgment) without the chain being visible in any one register. A63 fixes this by recording every analyst_judgment claim with hard-to-fake metadata: AnalystID (who), EmittedAt (when), UpstreamClaimRefs (≥1, parsed from JustificationRationale), ValidationStatus (pending|peer_reviewed|rejected). The bsa-no-new-claims-auditor cross-references A59 ClaimType=analyst_judgment rows against A63 to ensure every AJ claim has a corresponding A63 row + non-rejected ValidationStatus. Validation flow: governance.schemas.loader.iter_csv_rows(path) → list[dict]; each row validated against this schema.

AJID.description: Stable identifier for the analyst-judgment row. Format `AJ-NNN` (3-4 digit numeric, leading zeros allowed). Distinct from ClaimID — an AJ claim's ClaimID lives in A59, the AJ register entry has its own AJID for cross-row uniqueness + downstream traceability. The bsa-no-new-claims-auditor uses (AJID, ClaimID) pairs to detect drift between A59 and A63.

ClaimID.description: Foreign key to the A59 row whose ClaimType=analyst_judgment. MUST resolve in A59_claim_register.csv (enforced by x-bsa-foreign-key-refs). The A59 row's ClaimType field MUST be exactly 'analyst_judgment' (cross-checked by the bsa-no-new-claims-auditor at audit time, not at F5 hook time — F5 doesn't have the cross-row visibility to enforce A59.ClaimType lookups against this row's ClaimID).

AnalystID.description: Identifier of the analyst (or worker skill) that emitted the AJ claim. Free-form short string (operator initials, skill name, or analyst handle). Required so the audit trail records WHO is staking their epistemic credit on this claim. Empty values are rejected — anonymous analyst_judgment defeats the accountability the register exists for.

EmittedAt.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp when the AJ claim was first authored. Pattern enforcement mirrors the format hint because jsonschema's FormatChecker is advisory unless format-nongpl extras are installed. Used by downstream tools to filter recent AJ activity + by the auditor to detect 'AJ chains emitted within minutes of each other' (a pattern often indicative of compound inference rather than independent judgment).

UpstreamClaimRefs.description: Multi-valued FK to A59 ClaimIDs. ≥1 ClaimID required (per INV-07). Tokens delimited by `;` / `/` / whitespace, mirroring A59.SourceID convention. Each token MUST resolve in A59_claim_register.csv (enforced by x-bsa-foreign-key-refs with multi=true). The auditor additionally checks that NONE of the upstream ClaimIDs are themselves ClaimType=analyst_judgment (would create an AJ chain). If chaining is the analyst's deliberate intent, route via A51 with IssueType=decision_needed instead — A63 is for first-order judgments only.

ValidationStatus.description: Lifecycle state: 'pending' = freshly authored, awaiting peer review; 'peer_reviewed' = a peer reviewer (recorded in PeerReviewerID) has reviewed + accepted (convention: SHOULD be a different analyst from AnalystID, but v1.4.0 does NOT gate-enforce this — single-analyst engagements with external reviewers documented as `PeerReviewerID=external-reviewer-XYZ` are legitimate); 'rejected' = peer review found the AJ unjustified, claim should be retracted from A59 or routed via A51. Promote-time gate (in bsa-no-new-claims-auditor): every A59 ClaimType=analyst_judgment row used in H1/H4 packets MUST have a corresponding A63 row with ValidationStatus != 'rejected'. Pending is allowed (the audit doesn't block pre-promote on pending review — it surfaces the count for the operator to decide), but rejected is hard-block.

PeerReviewerID.description: Optional: identifier of the peer reviewer. REQUIRED (non-empty) when ValidationStatus=peer_reviewed (enforced by x-bsa-aj-validation-rules). Optional / typically empty for ValidationStatus=pending (no reviewer yet). Optional when ValidationStatus=rejected (the rejection rationale lives in Notes; recording the reviewer ID is recommended but not gate-enforced). Convention: SHOULD differ from AnalystID — self-review defeats the validation purpose, but v1.4.0 doesn't gate-enforce this (single-analyst engagements with external reviewers documented as `PeerReviewerID=external-reviewer-XYZ` are legitimate).

PeerReviewedAt.description: Optional: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of peer review. REQUIRED (non-empty) when ValidationStatus=peer_reviewed (enforced by x-bsa-aj-validation-rules). Optional / typically empty for ValidationStatus=pending (no reviewer yet). Optional when ValidationStatus=rejected (rejection timestamp may be derived from EmittedAt or recorded in Notes; not gate-enforced separately in v1.4.0).

Notes.description: Free-form analyst notes. For pending: optional context on what the AJ adds beyond the upstream claims. For peer_reviewed: optional reviewer comments. For rejected: REQUIRED non-empty rejection rationale (enforced by x-bsa-aj-validation-rules). Empty string is allowed for pending/peer_reviewed; the schema-level required-field check fires for absence, but minLength is not enforced for those statuses.

x-bsa-csv-columns-order._comment: Canonical column order for the A63 register CSV. Mirrors A51's pattern: ID first, then FK to A59, then audit-trail metadata, then optional review fields, then Notes last. F5 hook checks the header line against this order; mismatch is a hard-block.

x-bsa-uniqueness-rules._comment: EXECUTABLE at the F5 hook layer (v1.2.10 generic extension). AJID is the row-identifier; duplicate AJIDs would let two distinct rows collapse into one downstream and silently lose the audit trail.

x-bsa-foreign-key-refs._comment: EXECUTABLE at the F5 hook layer (v1.2.13 generic extension). Both ClaimID + UpstreamClaimRefs MUST resolve in A59_claim_register.csv. The auditor additionally cross-checks A59[ClaimID].ClaimType=='analyst_judgment' (cannot express in F5 hook — needs cross-row sibling read, deferred to bsa-no-new-claims-auditor).

foreign_keys.rationale: Every A63 row binds to exactly one A59 row whose ClaimType=analyst_judgment.

Each upstream ClaimID MUST exist in A59. Multi-valued (≥1; tokens delimited by ; / whitespace). The auditor additionally checks that none of the upstream rows are themselves ClaimType=analyst_judgment (anti-chaining).

x-bsa-aj-validation-rules._comment: EXECUTABLE at the F5 hook layer (v1.4.0 NEW). Cross-field rules the JSON Schema layer can't express directly. v1.4.0 ships TWO gate-enforced rules: (1) ValidationStatus=peer_reviewed → PeerReviewerID + PeerReviewedAt MUST be non-empty (otherwise the peer-review record is hollow). (2) ValidationStatus=rejected → Notes MUST be non-empty (rejection rationale required so the next analyst knows WHY the AJ was rejected). Self-review prevention (PeerReviewerID != AnalystID) and rejection-timestamp enforcement are intentionally NOT in this rules block — both are advisory / convention-only in v1.4.0; if pilot engagements show they're commonly violated, add as additional rules in a v1.4.x hotfix.
